records.finding: The bug-report template documented `shortfall <version> (<commit>)` unconditionally, but this diff makes the parenthesised commit conditional, and the case that drops it is the `go install` path the README recommends.
records.evidence: Template said '`shortfall version` prints `shortfall <version> (<commit>)`'. At base, main.go:36 printed that shape unconditionally; at head, formatVersionLine omits the parens when resolveBuild returns an empty commit, which it does for any module-proxy install.
records.reason: CONFIRMED in scope — unchanged doc bytes, but the diff changed the behavior the doc describes, which the examiner identified as the LIMIT of the earlier 'pre-existing text' precedent rather than an instance of it. Round 1. NOTE: .github/ is gate surface, forbidden on a feature branch by skills-policy 'Forbidden paths'; the founder was asked and explicitly waived it for this line so the doc and behavior land together (charter item 8). The PR body says so.

records.finding: goreleaser stamped {{.Version}}, which strips the leading 'v', while the new build-info path reports the module version with it — one binary, two version shapes.
records.evidence: '-X main.version={{.Version}}'; the published assets are shortfall_0.3.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz from the same template, so a release binary would print 'shortfall 0.3.0' where an installed one prints 'shortfall v0.3.0'. The test fixture ldVersion 'v0.3.0' encoded the wrong assumption and passed anyway, that arm being a passthrough.
records.reason: CONFIRMED in scope — the examiner verified the v-strip empirically against the published asset names and rejected the 'ldflags are pre-existing' defence, since at base ldflags were the ONLY real version source and there was no second shape to disagree with. Round 1.

records.finding: format.go's comment claims the flag help reads formatVocabulary, but main.go's usage() hardcodes text|json|markdown.
records.evidence: Comment: 'The flag help, the early rejection and the dispatcher all read it'. main.go usage() spelled the list out literally.
records.reason: REFUTED on the merits. The comment names three readers and all three genuinely read formatVocabulary: the flag package's help strings (impact.go:50, reconcile.go:36, both converted by this diff), knownFormat, and renderFormat. main.go's usage() is the top-level command banner, not flag help, and the comment never claimed it. Round 1. (The banner was nonetheless converted later for its own reasons — see the last finding.)

records.finding: The package doc says the package 'renders an engine.Report three ways' while this diff adds four exported symbols whose input is not an engine.Report.
records.evidence: doc.go: 'Package report renders an engine.Report three ways: JSON, the text ledger block, and markdown.'
records.reason: REFUTED, out of scope. RenderJSON/RenderText/RenderMarkdown all still take engine.Report and are untouched, so nothing became old. The sentence was already non-exhaustive at base — CustomersCSV and Summary both predate this diff and are named by neither the sentence nor the doc. Round 1.

records.finding: The {{.Tag}} fix for the release path regressed the snapshot path: .Tag ignores snapshot mode, and the dry-run job hands goreleaser the last root tag, so every snapshot binary would claim to BE the last release.
records.evidence: release.yml's snapshot job sets GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v[0-9]*'), a plain root tag; with -X main.version={{.Tag}} a snapshot from any untagged commit stamps v0.3.0, while the archive name_template still uses the SNAPSHOT-suffixed .Version — the same artifact named one thing and reporting another.
records.reason: CONFIRMED. This is a defect the PREVIOUS round's own fix introduced, which is exactly why the round was re-run rather than assumed good. Stamp is now v{{.Version}}: v-prefixed on release, and honestly 0.3.1-SNAPSHOT-<sha> on the dry run. TestReleaseStampIsVPrefixed pins all three shapes by reading .goreleaser.yaml. Round 2.

records.finding: The new usage() comment claimed the banner 'was the last statement of the vocabulary that formatVocabulary did not feed'. It was not — impact.go:64 still hardcoded the list.
records.evidence: Comment on an added line; an exhaustive grep of cmd/shortfall found exactly one surviving hardcoded enumeration, impact.go:64, byte-identical at base and head, while its twin reconcile.go:48 WAS converted in this same diff.
records.reason: CONFIRMED in scope — the comment is on added lines, and the author's own conversion of impact.go's twin puts subcommand usage lines inside the class the comment claimed was empty. Fixed by converting impact.go and restating the comment as an invariant rather than a superlative, then ENFORCING it: TestNoHardcodedFormatVocabulary builds its needle from formatUsage() so it carries no copy of the list, and mutation-testing confirms re-hardcoding impact.go reds it. Round 3.

records.finding: A test fixture comment said 'goreleaser stamps the TAG', contradicting .goreleaser.yaml's -X main.version=v{{.Version}}; the test name TestReleaseStampUsesTheTag asserted the opposite of itself.
records.evidence: Comment on added lines pointed the reader at two artifacts that both say the opposite: .goreleaser.yaml opens '# v{{.Version}}, not {{.Version}} and not {{.Tag}}', and the test's own third case asserts -X main.version={{.Tag}} is ABSENT.
records.reason: CONFIRMED on the COMMENT half only. The examiner split the finding: the docs-accuracy rule body excludes test names ('Do NOT flag: ... test names'), so the rename carried no rule weight and the .goreleaser.yaml citation resolves regardless. Comment corrected. The test was renamed to TestReleaseStampIsVPrefixed anyway — it is newly added in this diff and asserting the opposite of its own name, so leaving it because a rule excludes it would be knowingly shipping a misleading name. Round 3.
